title: A Typewriter for the Compass
premise: In 1911, Mirabel Dravenmoor, daughter of a disgraced pearl diver, works as a clerk for the Halloway Trading Company in a fog-bound port city, hiding her literacy and her name. When she is ordered to type a sealed letter, she discovers the company has framed her family for smuggling to cover its own debts—and that one berth on a departing ship offers escape from the reprisals coming for anyone with Dravenmoor blood. Torn between her father's pride, her brother's desperation, and her own longing to finally be seen, Mirabel forges documents, bargains with the company's ruthless secretary, and exposes the fraud at the cost of her anonymity. In the end, she gives the berth to her brother, stays behind to testify, and reclaims her family name—discovering that belonging was never something she could type her way into, only stand up and claim.
about_author: Felix Oyelaran is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trading-company ledgers from the early twentieth century. Their fiction draws on the faded ink of those records, giving voice to the clerks, divers, and indentured workers history filed away.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Hands
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She navigates her morning at Halloway Trading Company, typing invoices while concealing her identity as a diver's daughter. A near-discovery by a supervisor shows how fragile her invisibility is. Emotional beat: the exhausting discipline of being unseen.

chapters.title: Salt in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Flashback woven into present: her father's diving accident, the debt that bound the family to the company, and her mother's bargain to place Mirabel in the office. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into careful competence.

chapters.title: The Sealed Letter
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The company secretary, Mr. Voss, orders her to type a confidential letter naming 'the Dravenmoor operation' in a smuggling scheme. Her hands shake; she types it perfectly anyway. Emotional beat: terror masked as obedience.

chapters.title: Brother of the Tide
chapters.summary: Tobin's POV. Mirabel's brother works the docks, unaware he is named in company papers. He senses dockside tension, men asking questions about the Dravenmoors. Emotional beat: dread without understanding.

chapters.title: What the Ribbon Remembers
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She retrieves the carbon copy of the letter from the wastebasket, confirming the frame-up: the company itself moved the contraband. Emotional beat: the sick clarity of proof.

chapters.title: A Room Above the Chandlery
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She visits her father, who refuses to flee on principle—the sea gave him his living and his name. First open conflict between them. Emotional beat: love stiffened into stubbornness.

chapters.title: Voss Offers a Berth
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The secretary, needing a scapegoat handled quietly, dangles one berth on the Corvina, sailing in three weeks, for whichever Dravenmoor leaves quietly. Emotional beat: cold arithmetic dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Blood
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She calculates: father cannot dive again, Tobin has a wife and child coming, and she herself could vanish easiest. She begins drafting forged exit papers. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Forgery scenes; she studies Voss's hand, practices signatures, nearly caught by a night watchman. Emotional beat: the thrill and shame of becoming someone else on paper.

chapters.title: The Secretary's Own Ghost
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Backstory reveals Voss once took a berth like the one he now offers, abandoning a sister. His cruelty is a scar. Emotional beat: recognition of himself in Mirabel.

chapters.title: Tobin Learns the Truth
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Mirabel tells Tobin everything; he rages—at the company, at their father, at her for deciding alone. Emotional beat: fracture in the sibling bond.

chapters.title: The Harbor Watch
chapters.summary: Tobin's POV. Tobin surveils the company warehouse, gathering evidence of the smuggled pearls' route, wanting to fight rather than flee. Emotional beat: courage outpacing wisdom.

chapters.title: A Name Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At a harbor tavern, she publicly claims the Dravenmoor name for the first time in years to shield Tobin from an informant. Word spreads. Emotional beat: the terrifying relief of visibility.

chapters.title: Voss Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. With Mirabel exposed, Voss accelerates: the berth deadline shortens, and port authorities are tipped to arrest all Dravenmoors before the Corvina sails. Emotional beat: menace tightening.

chapters.title: Father's Last Dive
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Her father attempts one final dive to recover the pearl cache that proves the company's guilt—and fails, surfacing broken but alive, having seen the crates moved ashore. Emotional beat: sacrifice that buys truth, not safety.

chapters.title: The Forged Manifest
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Using her father's testimony and Tobin's observations, she completes a forged manifest proving Halloway shipped the contraband. She must plant it where authorities will find it. Emotional beat: steady hands over a pounding heart.

chapters.title: Bargain at Midnight
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Voss, dual focus. She confronts Voss privately, offering to disappear silently if he lets the manifest surface and clears the family name. He wavers, haunted by his own past. Emotional beat: two survivors negotiating the price of conscience.

chapters.title: One Berth, Three Names
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The choice crystallizes: only one can sail. Father refuses, Tobin's wife is due within the month. Mirabel decides it must be Tobin—and tells him so. Emotional beat: love as an act of decision, not feeling.

chapters.title: The Night Before Sailing
chapters.summary: Tobin's POV. Farewells at the dock; Tobin tries to refuse the berth, Mirabel holds firm. Father gives Tobin his diving knife. Emotional beat: sorrow braided with blessing.

chapters.title: Testimony in the Custom House
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Climax: as the Corvina departs, customs officers, armed with the manifest, raid Halloway. Mirabel testifies openly under her full name against Voss and the directors. Emotional beat: fear overcome by voice.

chapters.title: After the Fog Lifts
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Voss resigns rather than face trial, leaving her a final letter acknowledging what she chose that he could not. The family name is cleared; the company collapses. Emotional beat: vindication hollowed by cost.

chapters.title: A Typewriter for the Compass
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, months later. She works as a scrivener for freed divers' families, writing letters home for those who cannot. A letter arrives from Tobin across the sea. She signs her full name. Emotional beat: belonging claimed, not granted.
